22925-the-story-of-young-abraham-lincoln:
Wayne Whipple tells The Story of Young Abraham Lincoln for young readers. With all his brain and brawn, Whipple writes, Lincoln's real greatness lay in his heart. Whipple calls him the great-hearted man of the White House. Far more people know Lincoln's name, he adds, than ever met Bunyan's Great-Heart on the page.

The biography follows Lincoln from log-cabin childhood toward the presidency, stressing kindness, honesty, and hard study. Whipple shapes true events into episodes a child can hold, the rail fence, the borrowed book, the wrestling match. Such lives of Lincoln filled schoolrooms for decades. This one keeps the period's reverent tone, and its Bunyan comparison shows how Americans framed their hero.
abraham-lincoln: James Russell Lowell's 1864 essay on Abraham Lincoln: the poet-critic's tribute to the president in wartime. Eloquent and discerning, it saw Lincoln's greatness before it was fashionable. A classic of American political writing. Lowell's prose rises to its subject, and Lincoln emerges in full stature.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-eins: This 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia article on the Abbey of Einsiedeln — the Swiss shrine of the Black Madonna — recounts a thousand years of pilgrimage. George Cyprian Alston details its Baroque splendor. A central reference on Switzerland's holy mountain. The dark Madonna draws a million pilgrims a year.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-blessed-chris: A 1913 entry on Blessed Christine of Stommeln — the mystic of the Rhineland. Gabriel Meier honors her wondrous life. Her friendship with Peter of Dacia is famed. The stigmata marked her holy flesh. The beguine of the Cologne country. Her letters survive in the manuscripts.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-saint-hugh-of: St. Hugh of Lincoln was the Carthusian bishop. This entry traces his Witham, his Lincoln, and his sanctity. The swan's bishop: his tame swan guarded the saint at Stow in Lincolnshire's fens in the 1100s' decades of the Norman kings.
the-boys-life-of-abraham-lincoln: Helen Nicolay's 1906 biography of Lincoln written for young readers: the log cabin, the rail-splitting, the long road to the White House. Clear, inspiring, and full of anecdote, it presents Lincoln as the model American. A classic of children's biography.
the-life-of-abraham-lincoln: Henry Ketcham's biography brings Lincoln's story to young readers — the log cabin, the law office, the White House, and the martyrdom. Written with reverence and clarity, it presents the Great Emancipator as a model of honesty and perseverance. A classic introduction that inspired generations of American schoolchildren.
